clusters.headline: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say
clusters.summary: A truck carrying people to a funeral and a market alleged to be supplying fuel to the RSF were targeted.

clusters.headline: Australian MP Helen Haines loses both legs after car attack as suspect appears in court
clusters.summary: Doctors have amputated both of Helen Haines legs after the Australian lawmaker was hit in an apparent deliberate attack. The suspected driver involved in the attack has appeared in court.

clusters.headline: Gambia to pay victims of Yahya Jammeh's rule from proceeds of his seized US mansion
clusters.summary: The Gambia has confirmed receiving $2.5m from the sale of the house in Maryland.

clusters.headline: Kenya cult leader's children still being starved weeks before trial, son says
clusters.summary: Dan Mackenzie initially defended his father but now says he felt he had to report his own grandmother.

clusters.headline: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast
clusters.summary: Janine Lochrenberg, 65, was out on her daily morning swim with her club when she was attacked, her family tell the BBC.

clusters.headline: OCBC to become first non-Malaysian bank to allow Singapore saving accounts to hold ringgit from Oct 23
clusters.summary: Customers can spend the ringgit using OCBC debit cards or withdraw the currency at ATMs in Malaysia.

clusters.headline: Sudan: As Sudan War Spills Into Central African Republic, UN Warns Against Early Peacekeeper Exit
clusters.summary: [UN News] The UN warned on Tuesday against a premature withdrawal of its peacekeepers as the war in Sudan spills over into the Central African Republic (CAR).

clusters.headline: Nigeria: Presidential Panel Submits Draft National Policing Bill to Justice Ministry for Review
clusters.summary: [Premium Times] The proposed National Policing Bill seeks to establish the constitutional and legislative framework for a dual policing structure, comprising a Federal Police Service and State Police Services.

clusters.headline: Zimbabwe: Zimbabwe Faces Prolonged Fuel Cost Pressure As Oil Price Relief Unlikely Before 2028
clusters.summary: [263Chat] Zimbabwe's fuel-import-dependent economy could remain exposed to international oil market volatility into 2027 after the International Energy Agency (IEA) warned that global energy markets are unlikely to return to normal next year.

clusters.headline: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'
clusters.summary: The discovery of 12 women's bodies near Johannesburg has again highlighted South Africa's problem with violence against women.

clusters.headline: North Korea publishes photos of Kim Jong Un - why do rumours of his death keep coming back?
clusters.summary: North Korean state media has published photos of the dictator with his daughter after the unsubstantiated rumour spread.
